0.0.n: 違う describes 形 directly here, rather than meaning someone is wrong.

0.1.n: 違う形 describes a shape unlike the one being discussed.

0.2.n: の links the shape to the item that has it.

0.3.n: もの stands for an item without naming its type.

0.4.n: は sets the topic, while ね gently draws the listener into the explanation.

0.6.n: 使ってた shortens 使っていた, describing past ongoing or habitual use.

0.7.n: ん shortens の and introduces an explanatory tone before です.

0.8.n: です makes the explanation polite; the past tense is already expressed in 使ってた.

0.9.n: けど introduces the problem with the item previously used.

0.11.n: 大きい becomes 大きすぎる with すぎる, expressing excess; て connects this to the resulting problem.

0.12.n: 入ってなかった shortens 入っていなかった, describing a past state of not fitting inside.

0.13.n: ん adds an explanatory tone to the statement about not fitting.

0.14.n: です keeps the explanation polite without changing the past tense of 入ってなかった.

0.15.n: けど leaves the thought open, preparing for the contrast with the new item.

1.0.n: これ refers to the item the speaker is showing or discussing.

1.1.n: が identifies this item as the one being praised.

1.2.n: ね invites the listener's attention and gives the statement a conversational feel.

1.4.n: めちゃめちゃ is a casual, emphatic intensifier used here with ベスト.

1.5.n: ベスト is borrowed from English and describes the speaker's ideal choice.

1.6.n: で connects the description ベスト to the next statement.

1.8.n: めっちゃ is a casual intensifier emphasizing how much the container holds.

1.9.n: 入る describes things going inside; the things that fit are left unstated.

1.10.n: ん gives the claim an explanatory tone before the polite ending.

1.11.n: です makes this otherwise casual-sounding explanation polite.

1.12.n: よ emphasizes information the speaker wants the listener to notice.

2.0.n: 多分 signals that the speaker is estimating rather than making a certain claim.

2.1.n: ダイソー is the name of a Japanese discount retail chain.

2.2.n: さん is attached to the store name as a friendly, respectful way to refer to the company.

2.3.n: の links Daiso to 中, establishing the range being compared.

2.4.n: 中 literally means inside; here it refers to the range of items sold at Daiso.

2.5.n: でも combines with 中 to highlight a comparison within Daiso's selection.

2.7.n: この must come before a noun, unlike これ, which stands alone.

2.8.n: 透明 describes the container's see-through appearance and takes な before a noun.

2.9.n: な connects 透明 to もの so it can describe the item.

2.10.n: もの refers to the container without explicitly naming it.

2.12.n: 円 is the Japanese currency unit, following the amount.

2.13.n: 以下 includes the stated limit, so items costing exactly 300 yen also count.

2.14.n: の links the price limit to the items it describes.

2.15.n: 物 refers to the products in the price range being compared.

2.16.n: で marks the comparison group: items costing 300 yen or less.

2.17.n: は highlights that comparison group, limiting the claim to those items.

2.18.n: 一番 before 大きい makes the description a superlative: largest within the specified group.

2.19.n: 大きくって is a conversational version of 大きくて, connecting the size description to what follows.

3.0.n: これ refers back to the container being recommended.

3.1.n: に marks the destination where the items are put away.

3.2.n: ね adds a friendly pause while keeping the listener engaged.

3.4.n: 収納してたら shortens 収納していたら; たら introduces the situation in which the speaker discovered the good result.

3.5.n: めちゃめちゃ casually strengthens the positive judgment that follows.

3.6.n: 良かった is the past form of 良い, evaluating the result of using the container.

3.7.n: ので connects the successful storage experience to the decision to buy more.

3.9.n: これ refers to the same type of container, not another purchase of the exact same physical object.

3.10.n: を marks the container type as what the speaker bought.

3.11.n: ね creates a conversational pause after identifying what was bought.

3.13.n: 3 combines with つ to state how many containers were purchased.

3.14.n: つ is a general counting suffix; 3つ counts three objects without naming their category.

3.15.n: 追加 indicates that these purchases add to containers the speaker already owns.

3.16.n: で makes 追加 describe how the purchase relates to the existing collection.

3.17.n: 購入しました combines 購入 with the polite past form of する; it sounds more formal than 買いました.

0.lit: A differently shaped one, I was using, but it was too big and wasn't fitting inside, but…
0.tip: Both 使ってた and 入ってなかった drop い from longer forms, a very common feature of casual speech.

1.lit: This one, you know, is absolutely best, and so much fits inside, I'm telling you.
1.tip: 入る describes things fitting inside, so めっちゃ入る naturally means the container holds a lot.

2.lit: Probably even among Daiso's selection, this transparent item, among items 300 yen or less, is biggest, and…
2.tip: 以下 includes the stated amount: 300円以下 means 300 yen or less, not strictly under 300 yen.

3.lit: When storing things in this, it was really good, so I purchased three of these additionally.
3.tip: Here, たら means when rather than if: the speaker is reporting a result discovered through actual use.
